# Detailed presentation characters

Source: Microsoft Rocketbox Avatar Library, https://github.com/microsoft/Microsoft-Rocketbox

Original assets: `Female_Adult_07`, `Male_Adult_12`, `Female_Adult_03`, `Male_Adult_01`, `Male_Adult_04`, `Female_Adult_10`. Copyright (c) 2020 Microsoft. Distributed under MIT; the complete notice accompanies these assets in `LICENSE.md`.

Anansi adaptation: Blender import, relaxed arm pose, material conversion, garment material separation, texture resizing/compression, canonical orientation, idle breathing and GLB export. Optional fitted glasses, sunglasses, hoop earrings and a wrist bracelet were modelled for this presentation and bound to the skeleton. Real footwear variants retain source mesh geometry and textures: Male_Adult_01 low-tops, Male_Adult_04 high-tops, Female_Adult_07 tall boots. They are re-pivoted at the foot joints for fitting. The earlier rounded procedural shoes are hidden/unused and no longer offered. Source copies: character-{female,male,bob,polo,curls,covered}.blend in the presentation deliverable folder.

These are licensed modelled characters, not scans of guests and not original Anansi character designs. They are fictional presentation visitors. Facial features, hairstyle geometry, facial-hair shapes and garment cuts remain preset-specific. No race/ethnicity field or inferred race labels are used. Independent face sculpting, garment swaps, fitted body morphs and walking animation are not implemented. Build is a subtle width adjustment, not a body morph.

Presentation appearance controls now offer independent skin-tone and hair-colour palettes, plus original-colour resets. Runtime atlas masks and material shaders preserve original texture detail and avoid recolouring the eye atlas, lips, clothing and head covering. Covered-hair presets do not expose a hair-colour control. The palettes are appearance choices, not race labels. Hair-colour changes do not change hairstyle geometry or replace baked-in beards. Choices save in browser-local storage and are shared by the look preview, seating avatar and photo keepsakes; no backend is involved. Garment colours remain texture tints, not replacement garment textures.
